sources.title: Andrei Sakharov, Memoirs (English translation, 1990) -- his own firsthand account
Nobel Peace Prize 1975 citation and Nobel lecture (delivered by Yelena Bonner in his absence)

analytical_rigor.rationale: Documented, named theoretical contributions to Soviet thermonuclear weapon design ('Sakharov's Third Idea', the layered-cake fission-fusion-fission concept) and the tokamak fusion-reactor concept -- attested by the surviving technical record, not self-report.

independent_thinking.rationale: Documented public opposition to the Soviet Academy's nomination of a Lysenko-aligned scientist in 1964, and the 1968 essay 'Reflections on Progress, Peaceful Coexistence, and Intellectual Freedom' circulated via samizdat against explicit institutional pressure -- both dated, named, independently corroborated acts of open dissent from state orthodoxy.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Sustained 12 years as an openly recognized dissident (1968-1980) under continuous state press campaigns, KGB surveillance, and Academy pressure, escalating to arrest and internal exile to Gorky in 1980 -- an unusually long, well-documented pattern of tolerating direct institutional conflict rather than a single incident.

persistence.rationale: Two separate documented hunger strikes (1984, 1985) while held in internal exile, each sustained through force-feeding and isolation, specifically to secure his wife's medical travel -- dated, corroborated, repeated behavior under severe state pressure.

autonomy_need.rationale: Inferred from the documented transition from a state-employed, privileged weapons scientist to an independent public dissenter at severe personal cost -- a specific, sourced career reversal rather than a generic personality claim.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Documented, repeated acceptance of severe personal and professional risk (loss of the highest state privileges, internal exile, forced feeding) in pursuit of stated principles -- scored dual-edged since the same risk tolerance produced both the courageous public record and years of serious harm to himself and his family.

achievement_drive.rationale: Inferred from sustained output across two entirely different arenas at the highest level (leading thermonuclear weapon design, then internationally recognized human-rights advocacy culminating in the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize).

impact_motivation.rationale: Documented shift from classified weapons work to writing appeals for over 200 individually named political prisoners and co-founding the Committee on Human Rights in the USSR (1970) -- inferred motivation toward broad social impact from this specific, sourced body of advocacy work.

leadership_drive.rationale: Co-founded the Committee on Human Rights in the USSR (1970) and, after 1986, co-led the Inter-Regional Deputies Group in the new Soviet parliament -- two named, dated instances of taking organizing leadership rather than remaining a solitary dissenting voice.

adaptability.rationale: Inferred from his documented return to active political participation in 1989 immediately upon release from years of internal exile, including direct fact-finding travel to Armenia and Azerbaijan despite advanced age and prior health strain.

belief_updating.rationale: Documented substantive change of public position from weapons-program insider to advocate for arms-control and human rights over the late 1950s-1960s, corroborated by his own dated 1967-1968 writings rather than reconstructed later.

social_assertiveness.rationale: Documented as regularly holding press conferences with Western correspondents in his own apartment from the early 1970s -- inferred willingness to speak publicly, though most direct-quote evidence in the record is written (letters, essays) rather than observed public speech.

collaboration.rationale: Documented sustained partnership with his wife Yelena Bonner across the entire dissident period, and co-founding work with Valery Chalidze and Andrei Tverdokhlebov -- narrower evidence base than for other attributes, kept at inference level.

provenance.notes: Roster-17 intake (2026-09). Wikidata identity verified live (Q997) before scoring. Evidence drawn from a live Wikipedia fetch, cross-referenced against the known existence of his own published Memoirs and the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize record. Deliberately scored to only 13 attributes this pass -- his documented record is unusually deep in conviction/conflict/persistence-type traits but genuinely thin in this cycle's research on thinking-style and creativity-facet attributes (curiosity, systems_abstraction, cross_domain_range were considered but not scored without a stronger source on his specific physics working style, not just his physics achievements).

holdReason: Only 13 scored attributes (need 18); coverage 0.39 below the 0.6 threshold; 10 attributes at confidence>=0.5 (need 12). Genuinely evidence-limited by this cycle's single-source (Wikipedia) research pass, not by weak underlying evidence -- his documented record on conviction/conflict/persistence attributes is strong; thinking-facet attributes (curiosity, analytical_rigor, systems_abstraction) were not scored because this cycle's research did not surface strong enough sourcing on his specific physics working style. A deeper research pass (his own Memoirs, more physics-specific biography) would likely close this gap without changing any already-scored row.
